```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
withr::with_dir(here::here(), targets::tar_load(lab_08_workbook))

baseline <- read_csv(here::here("files", "data", "mindspark", "ms_blel_jpal_baseline.csv"),
                     show_col_types = FALSE)
endline <- read_csv(here::here("files", "data", "mindspark", "ms_blel_jpal_endline.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)
treated <- semi_join(filter(baseline, treat == 1), endline, by = "st_id")
```

Bring a calculator, your notes, and a laptop per pair if you can. For part 3, [download the workbook](/files/labs/lab-08.xlsx) ([how to open it](index.qmd#opening-a-workbook)).

## 1. Individual check (15 minutes)

The lab starts with a 15-minute individual check on t-tests for two samples. You work on your own, on paper. As on the exams, you can use any print materials, including your notes, and a calculator, but no other devices. The check is worth 10 points (see the [syllabus](/syllabus.qmd#quizzes)).

## 2. Your questions and the key ideas

Pritha goes over the check and takes your questions. Then she goes over the key ideas again: a gain as one number per student, the paired t-test as a one-sample t-test on gains, and the ANOVA table. For SS between, we add up n(M − overall mean)² across the groups, and the book uses ΣT²/n − G²/N. Both give the same number. Where we write η̂², the book writes η².

## 3. Real data, in pairs (about 18 minutes)

Did the Mindspark students gain about the same at all three centers? The workbook holds the `r nrow(treated)` students the lottery picked for Mindspark who took both tests. In the `students` sheet, each gain is the endline score minus the baseline score. The `gains` sheet holds the same gains, one column per center.

In the `groups` sheet, rows 2, 3 and 6 are filled in. Type rows 4 and 5 in column B, then copy B4:B5 to C4:D5:

| Row | What | Formula |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | SS | `=DEVSQ(gains!A:A)` |
| 5 | n × (M − overall mean)² | `=B2*(B3-$B$6)^2` |

`DEVSQ` adds up the squared deviations from the mean, so it gives SS. Then fill in the `table` sheet. The df and the total SS are filled in:

| Cell | What | Formula |
|---|---|---|
| B2 | SS between | `=SUM(groups!B5:D5)` |
| B3 | SS within | `=SUM(groups!B4:D4)` |
| D2 | MS between | `=B2/C2` |
| D3 | MS within | `=B3/C3` |
| E2 | F | `=D2/D3` |
| F2 | p | `=F.DIST.RT(E2, C2, C3)` |
| B5 | η̂² | `=B2/B4` |

a. At which center did the Mindspark students gain the most, on average?
b. Check: do SS between and SS within add up to the total SS?
c. What are F and p? What's your decision at α = 0.05?
d. Does your decision show that the Mindspark students gained equally at all three centers? Would it tell us where the program worked best?

## 4. Your sentence (about 5 minutes)

On a slip of paper with your name, write one sentence: what does F tell us about the three centers? Hand it to Pritha. A real attempt earns the lab's 3 points. It doesn't have to be correct.
